Senses.Explanation: To pronounce a case settled on the evidence or confession already supplied. Masters use the courtroom formula when delivering a decisive appraisal of a story, speaker, or ritual occasion. Baiyu Jingsi says that Śākyamuni and Ānanda are both disreputable and closes their case from the facts. Miaoyun Zhenxiong says his preceding words have already closed the case before requesting a further memorial phrase. Baichi Xingyuan quotes his teacher accepting an unnamed monk’s auspicious response as enough to close the case. Sanshan Denglai describes exposing the buddha-seat’s stolen goods and then closing the case. Shending Yikui says Xuansha’s appraisal closed the case but left an injustice still requiring redress.
